summary: Nathan Sivin was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the Defense Language Institute, MIT, Harvard, and Kyoto University. He taught at MIT from 1966 to 1977 and later served at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–2006).

Nathan W. Hill specializes in Tibetology, linguistics, and sinology. He earned his degree at Harvard under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff, later serving as Principal Investigator at SOAS (~2008–2019) and Trinity College Dublin (~2019, 2021).
Nathaniel Brassey Halhed worked in indology and linguistics. He was educated at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford, and served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, having also studied under the traditional teacher Khenpo Namdrol.
Nathaniel Grove works in Tibetology and computational fields. He was affiliated with the University of Virginia in 2006 and held a post there as Research Associate in 2026.

Nathaniel Tarn worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, Paris, and Chicago, holding posts at the London School of Economics (~1958–1960), SOAS (~1960–1967), Princeton (1970), and Rutgers University (1972–1985).

Nathmal Tatia was an indology and philosophy scholar who earned a Doctor of Literature at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee and Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982–1990).
Navina Lamminger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Ngawang Thokmey works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as South Asian bibliographer at the University of Virginia (attested 2003–2008) and later at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Nawang Tsering is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under Lal Mani Joshi and served as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).
Neal Donner is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).
Neelima Mundayar is a scholar in religious studies and indology. As of 2026, she is a PhD student at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Wilfried Swenden.

Nenghai Shi was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Peking University and under Kecheng Zhang, Foyuan, Guanyi, and Khangsar Rinpoche, later serving as vice-president of the Buddhist Association of China (1953–1966).
Ng-Fung Yuen works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of the West under the supervision of Kottegoda Warnasuriya (attested 2009).
Ngakchang Gönpo Tsé Ten studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Ngan-che Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Jing Yin, having also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007).
Ngawang Jinpa is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995).
Ngawang Jorden works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a post at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.
Ngawang Lek Shé Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Ngawang Norbu studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
